questions.text: "___ consequentialism offers genuine insights, it faces serious objections about rights." (concessive clause)
questions.hint: "Although + clause" = concessive conjunction

questions.text: "The argument is compelling. ___, it faces serious objections about individual dignity." (concessive adverb)
questions.hint: Concessive adverb after full stop

questions.text: "___ ___ the action saved many lives, using a person as a means would remain wrong." (concessive conditional)
questions.hint: "Even if X, Y still holds" = concessive conditional

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ ___, the core argument is not undermined." (formal: even if all that is true)
questions.hint: "Be that as it may" = formal phrase granting all objections before asserting main point

questions.text: "___ ___ that this argument has weaknesses." (acknowledging before countering)
questions.hint: "Admittedly X. [That said / Nevertheless, Y]" = concede before countering

questions.text: "___ ___ that outcomes never matter, but only that they cannot override all constraints." (precise qualification)
questions.hint: "I am not claiming X, but only Y" = limiting your claim precisely

questions.text: "___ these objections, care ethics makes a genuinely important contribution." (formal — despite)
questions.hint: "Notwithstanding + noun" = formal equivalent of "despite"

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ ___, we may conclude that no single ethical framework is fully adequate." (drawing conclusion)
questions.hint: "In light of the above" = formal conclusion based on preceding discussion

questions.text: "Consequentialism focuses on outcomes, ___ deontology focuses on the nature of the act." (sharp contrast)
questions.hint: "Whereas" = sharp contrast between two opposites in one sentence

questions.text: "___ ___ objection to this view is that it generates paradoxical conclusions." (introducing counter at its strongest)
questions.hint: "The strongest objection to this view is…" = charitable introduction of counter-argument

questions.text: What is consequentialism?
opts: The view that actions are right if they conform to moral duties
The view that the moral value of an action is determined by its consequences
The view that character determines right action
The view that context and relationships are primary
questions.correct: The view that the moral value of an action is determined by its consequences
questions.hint: Reading 1: consequentialism

questions.text: "The argument is persuasive ___ ___ ___. It breaks down in extreme cases." (= true within limits)
questions.hint: "Up to a point / to some extent / in certain respects" all express partial agreement

questions.text: "___ granting the force of this criticism, the overall case for my position stands." (concede + counter)
questions.hint: "Even granting X, Y still holds"

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ objection — I acknowledge its point — but it does not succeed."
opts: The point is well taken as an
questions.hint: "The point is well taken" = acknowledging validity before countering

questions.text: What is "compatibilism" in the free will debate?
opts: The view that free will and determinism are incompatible
The view that free will does not exist
The view that free will and determinism are compatible — freedom means acting from your own values
The view that quantum indeterminacy provides genuine freedom
questions.correct: The view that free will and determinism are compatible — freedom means acting from your own values
questions.hint: Reading 2: compatibilism

questions.text: "___ ___ of this argument is that moral philosophy needs multiple frameworks." (practical conclusion)
questions.hint: "The upshot is that…" = the practical conclusion

questions.text: Which uses a concessive structure INCORRECTLY?
opts: "Although the argument is powerful, it has limitations."
"Even though consequences matter, they are not all that matters."
"Although the argument is powerful, but it has limitations."
"While deontology respects persons, consequentialism respects outcomes."
questions.correct: "Although the argument is powerful, but it has limitations."
questions.hint: "Although X, Y" — never "although + clause + but + clause" together

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ is that no single ethical framework resolves all moral dilemmas." (drawing a conclusion)
questions.hint: "What this shows is that…" = conclusion phrase from philosophical argument

questions.text: What is the "trolley problem"?
opts: A real historical event involving a trolley accident
A famous thought experiment exploring moral intuitions about dilemmas
A consequentialist argument for always saving the most lives
A deontological rule about not harming individuals
questions.correct: A famous thought experiment exploring moral intuitions about dilemmas
questions.hint: Listening 3: Nour introduces the trolley problem

questions.text: "___ ___ that X. Nevertheless, this does not establish Y." (the full pattern)
opts: Any pattern with "admittedly" or "it is true"
questions.correct: Any pattern with "admittedly" or "it is true"
questions.hint: "It is true that X / Admittedly, X. Nevertheless, Y." = concede then counter

questions.text: "___ ordinary situations, the principle holds. ___ extreme dilemmas, it may require qualification." (distinguishing contexts)
questions.hint: "In ordinary situations X; in extreme cases Y"

questions.text: The ethical framework associated with Jeremy Bentham and John Stuart Mill, judging actions by their consequences, is called ___.
questions.hint: Reading 1: consequentialism

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ objection to my view is that partiality can lead to nepotism." (introducing counter)
questions.hint: "The strongest objection to X is…" = steelmanning the opposing view

questions.text: "Notwithstanding these objections, the argument holds" is a formal way of saying "despite these objections."
questions.hint: "Notwithstanding" = formal equivalent of "despite/in spite of"

questions.text: What is a "moral dilemma"?
opts: A situation where all choices are clearly right or wrong
A mathematical problem in ethical theory
A situation where there are genuine conflicts between legitimate moral considerations
A type of philosophical argument used to challenge beliefs
questions.correct: A situation where there are genuine conflicts between legitimate moral considerations
questions.hint: Listening 3: Nour and Aleksei's conclusion
